question: The Konark Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1984) situated in Puri district, Odisha, dedicated to the Sun God (Surya), was built by which ruler, and is designed to represent what symbolic concept?
option_1: Narasimhadeva I; a chariot with 24 wheels (24 hours of the day), pulled by 7 horses (7 days of the week)
option_2: Rajaraja I; a temple tower representing the 12 months of the year
option_3: Krishna I; a monolithic temple representing the 9 planets
option_4: Kumaragupta I; a stepwell representing the lunar calendar
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narasimhadeva I; a chariot with 24 wheels (24 hours of the day), pulled by 7 horses (7 days of the week).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Konark Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1984) situated in Puri district, Odisha, dedicated to the Sun God (Surya), was built by Narasimhadeva I.

 

• It is designed as a chariot-shaped temple with 12 pairs of wheels (24 wheels total), symbolising the 24 hours of the day, and is depicted as being pulled by 7 horses, symbolising the 7 days of the week.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Konark Sun Temple's intricate stone carvings and its symbolic representation of time through its chariot design make it one of the most architecturally significant and celebrated temples in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajaraja I, Krishna I, and Kumaragupta I (Options 2, 3, 4) are rulers associated with other monuments (Brihadeeswarar Temple, Kailasa Temple, and Nalanda University respectively), not the Konark Sun Temple, which was built by Narasimhadeva I.

question: Which of the following correctly identifies the year in which Dholavira, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Kutch district, Gujarat, and part of the Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization, was inscribed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2021.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dholavira, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Kutch district, Gujarat, and part of the Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization, was inscribed in 2021.

 

• It was discovered by J.P. Joshi (1967–68), and is considered to have the most advanced water system in the Harappan civilization (large reservoirs, step wells, and rainwater harvesting).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dholavira's sophisticated water conservation system, including its network of reservoirs and stepwells, reflects the advanced urban planning capabilities of the Harappan civilization in an arid region.

 

NOTE

 

• 2016, 2019, and 2023 (Options 1, 2, 4) do not match Dholavira's documented year of UNESCO inscription, which is specifically 2021.

question: 'Kutiyattam (Koodiyattam)', a Sanskrit theatre tradition from Kerala performed in a temple theatre called 'Koothambalam', and considered one of the oldest surviving theatre forms (2000+ years), uses which of the following documented techniques?

solution_text:
The correct answer is Elaborate facial expressions (Rasa-Abhinaya) and codified hand gestures (Mudras).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

Additional Information
